status_summary: PPO is documented as a clearance point for some political staffing. An OPM memo of 2025-04-10 (page 2) states that approving or withdrawing an agency's Schedule C appointing authority requires preclearance from the White House Office of Presidential Personnel, and OPM's release of 2025-07-29 on Schedule G says PPO gives final review and approval of agency requests. EO 14356 (signed 2025-10-15) sets agency strategic hiring committees and exempts Schedule C and Schedule G positions without naming PPO, and EO 14410 (signed 2026-06-03) routes Schedule Policy/Career position recommendations through the OPM Director to the President, with no mention of PPO in the readable text. Dan Scavino was named in August 2025 to lead PPO in place of Sergio Gor, and on 2025-09-11 the Senate changed its rules to allow most executive nominees to be confirmed in batches (41 on 2025-09-18 and 74 on 2025-10-07). Reporting on nominee vetting, confirmation pace and turnover rests on news sources, and a PPO role in firings of political appointees was not documented.

timeline.event: OPM Acting Director Charles Ezell issues a memo to agency heads, Schedule C Terms of Employment Flexibilities, which says approving or withdrawing an agency's Schedule C appointing authority requires preclearance from the White House Office of Presidential Personnel (routed through the agency's White House Liaison) in addition to approval by OPM's White House Liaison, and that Schedule C appointments should not advance without coordinating with the agency White House Liaison.

Eight senators write to the acting OPM director asking for written information on PPO's role in hiring Schedule C appointees; they say the April memo encouraged higher salaries and a bypass of standard hiring review, which they argue would let appointees start without vetting.
OPM issues Schedule G guidance routing agency requests through OPM's Executive and Schedule C System with final review and approval by the White House Office of Presidential Personnel.
The White House names deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino to lead PPO in place of Sergio Gor, who had been nominated the previous week as ambassador to India; no effective date was given.
The Senate changes its rules by majority vote to allow bundled consideration of most executive branch nominees; it then confirms 41 nominees in one batch on 2025-09-18 and 74 on 2025-10-07.

EO 14356 (signed 2025-10-15, published in the Federal Register 2025-10-20) requires each agency to set up a strategic hiring committee (deputy head, chief of staff and designees) to approve filling each vacancy, with notice to OPM; section 3(a)(iv) exempts Schedule C and Schedule G positions, and the text does not use the term Presidential Personnel.
OPM publishes the final rule letting agencies move policy-influencing positions into Schedule Policy/Career (effective 2026-03-09); agencies petition OPM, which recommends positions to the President.

EO 14410 (signed 2026-06-03, published 2026-06-10 at 91 FR 34893) transfers the positions listed in its appendix into Schedule Policy/Career and has agency heads petition the OPM Director, who recommends further positions to the President (section 3(a)(ii)); the text read does not mention Presidential Personnel, and the appendix was available only as images.

title: Run political staffing through a strong Presidential Personnel Office
uncertainties: The OPM Schedule C memo (dated 2025-04-10) was read on opm.gov; the Schedule G guidance was read as an OPM release, not as the underlying guidance document. The March 2025 vetting description and figures rest on a Bloomberg article that relies on unnamed people and a White House official. The Breitbart piece is a favorable account built on White House-provided figures and statements from officials, not independently verified. The Scavino handover date is not established: the AP report of 2025-08-26 says he will take over and Brookings later reports him as Gor's successor. Whether PPO has a role in choosing the positions placed in Schedule Policy/Career is not shown by the text of EO 14410 (an unofficial rendition of the text was read; the appendix was not). Overlap with c03-01 and c03-07 (Schedule Policy/Career) is intended; this record tracks only PPO's role. The progress figure of 55 is a judgment: PPO's clearance role is documented, but its authority over firings and over agency hiring generally is not. News reports that describe practices or counts rather than a dated government action are not listed as timeline events: Bloomberg via Fortune (2025-03-06) on PPO loyalty vetting, Brookings (2025-11-24) on 216 confirmations at day 300, Government Executive (2026-07-23) on a record pace of departures and Breitbart (2026-08-21) with unverified White House figures; they remain cited as sources. The naming of Dan Scavino (2025-08-26, reported by the Associated Press) and the Senate's 2025-09-11 rule change (reported by Brookings) are kept as timeline events because they are government actions. The Federal Register API confirmed EO 14356 (document 2025-19614, published 2025-10-20) and EO 14410 (document 2026-11594, 91 FR 34893, published 2026-06-10, signed 2026-06-03). The EO 14410 appendix is available only as images and was not read.
